newsitem.title: USA: Great Bay status questioned by NRC.
newsitem.headline: Great Bay status questioned by NRC.

text.p: Great Bay Power Corp said Monday the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission staff stated it believes the company does not currently satisfy the commission's definition of "electric utility."

The NRC has issued a temporary exemption allowing Great Bay six months to establish itself as an electric utility, the company said. If it were unable to do so, Great Bay would have to satisfy nuclear power plant decommission funding requirements applicable to non-electric utilities.

The company said this would mean providing a surety bond or other decommissioning funding mechanism allowed by the NRC. As an electric utility, Great Bay satisfies the NRC decommissioning requirements with payments of about $92,000 per month.

The company also said it has received all shareholder and regulatory approvals for the formation of a holding company structure and will form BayCorp Holdings Ltd effective Tuesday. The new stock, which will be exchanged share-for-share for Great Bay common, will begin trading on the American Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
